---
title: "Holding patterns"
description: "How OPDI finds holding patterns (holding-start, holding-end) and measures their duration, distance and number of circuits."
---

## In one sentence

A holding pattern is a loop flown while the aircraft waits for permission to
continue, usually before landing; OPDI publishes each one as a pair of events,
`holding-start` and `holding-end`, with three measurements.

## What it needs

- The cleaned positions, barometric altitude, heading and ground speed of the
  track's reports, about one every 5 s.
- The elevation of the destination airport, and the go-arounds, take-off and
  landing times of the same track. The departure and destination airports
  are those the flight list publishes, after its correction by the runway
  events (see [Correction from the runway events](airports.qmd#correction-from-the-runway-events)): a flight
  whose destination the runway events change has its holds read as an
  arrival at the airport it landed at.

## How it is computed

A hold turns through at least one nearly complete circle, always in the same
direction, stays in a small area and keeps roughly one level. Turns given by
controllers to space aircraft alternate left and right, a go-around climbs
away, and a circuit flown by a light aircraft is low and slow.

1. **Turn per report.** For each report, take the change of heading since the
   last report with a heading, between −180° and +180°. A change across a
   silence of more than 60 s, or faster than 6° per second, is ignored. A
   report is **turning** at 0.4° per second or more.
2. **Window test.** Over a sliding window of 360 s (6 minutes), the window is
   flagged when all of these hold:
   - the turn, counted with its sign, adds up to at least 300° in one
     direction;
   - at least 80% of all turning is in that direction;
   - the first and last positions of the window are at most 8 NM apart;
   - the aircraft flew at least 15 NM in the window;
   - the altitude changed by at most 2,500 ft in total (the sum of all ups and
     downs).

   The window is placed three ways (ending at the report, starting at it and
   centred on it), so an orbit shorter than the window is still seen whole. A
   window whose two ends are not 0.8 to 1.25 window lengths apart in time,
   because of a silence inside it, is not judged.
3. **Height and speed.** A flagged report counts only at least 2,500 ft above
   the airport and at least 140 kt over the ground.
4. **Episodes.** Flagged reports less than 120 s apart form one episode. It
   starts and ends at its first and last report turning in its main
   direction, so a lead-in turn the other way is not counted.
5. **Keep or drop.** An episode is kept when it lasts at least 240 s and its
   turn adds up to at least 330°. It is dropped when it starts or ends within
   180 s of a `go-around` of the same track: repeated approaches are not holds.
6. **Pattern.** The hold is an `orbit` when less than 15% of its reports are
   straight, otherwise a `racetrack` (two straight legs joined by two half
   circles).
7. **Context.** `info.context` is `arrival` when the flight lands at its
   destination at most 60 minutes after the hold, which ends at most 150 NM
   from that airport; `en-route` when it lands, but later or further away;
   and `other` for a local flight (departure equal to destination, or no
   destination), no landing after the hold, three or more holds on the track,
   or holds making up more than half of the time in the air. Aerial work,
   survey, firefighting and training flights that circle fall under `other`.
8. **Altitude.** The altitude of the two events comes from the first and last
   report of the hold that has one.

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI, as a rule rather than a trained model. Parts of it come
  from published detectors:
  - the turning threshold of 0.4° per second and the test that a hold turns
    one way come from the holding detection of
    [US patent 11,935,419](../resources.qmd#ref-boeing-patent);
  - the shortest hold, 4 minutes, is the minimum holding time of the
    rule-based detector of [Melo (2023)](../resources.qmd#ref-melo-2023), which finds holds
    where the track flies back over itself instead of summing its turns;
  - the window of 6 minutes, meant to hold one holding circuit, is the same
    as that of the neural-network detector of
    [Olive, Basora, Sun and Spinielli (2024)](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2024), included in the
    [`traffic`](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2019) library.
- The rule was checked against the hand-corrected holding labels of
  [Olive, Basora, Sun and Spinielli (2024)](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2024), made on the
  arrival trajectories of [Olive, Basora and Sun (2022)](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-data-2022).
  Holding procedures are defined in ICAO Doc 8168, PANS-OPS
  ([as referenced by the Irish AIP](../resources.qmd#ref-airnav-enr15)).
- Study: [Holding, point merge and FIR crossings as flight events](../../papers/airspace-events-v1/index.html).

## What is published

Event types `holding-start` (first report of the hold) and `holding-end`
(last report), with position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and
`time_passed_s`. Both carry in `info`: `holding_seq`, `pattern`, `direction`
(`R` or `L`), `circuits`, `duration_s`, `distance_nm`, `altitude_start_ft`,
`altitude_end_ft`, `straight_pct` and `context` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

Three measurements are set on `holding-end` only:

| Measurement | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `holding_duration_s` | Time in the hold, in seconds. |
| `holding_distance_nm` | Distance flown in the hold, in NM. |
| `holding_circuits` | Number of loops: the total turn divided by 360°, to one decimal. |

## Use cases

- **Holding delay before landing per airport**: the sum of
  `holding_duration_s` of the holds with `info.context` = `arrival`, per day.
- **Where aircraft hold**: the positions and altitudes of `holding-start`,
  which show the holding stacks of an airport.
- **Extra fuel**: `holding_distance_nm` per aircraft type, as an input to fuel
  estimates.

## Limitations

Circling for other reasons (aerial work, training) meets the definition: use
`info.context`. Holds below 2,500 ft above the airport or flown slower than
140 kt are not found. See
[Limitations: holding](../limitations.qmd#lim-holding).
